thread:
Ryan (support): Heads up — we're seeing a sudden spike of 503s for the hosted /v1/generate endpoint affecting a handful of customers (notably acme-inc). Error rate ~8% over the last 15m. Customers report requests timing out then the API returning 503. Logs show upstream inference worker exits and container restarts on gpu-7. Escalating to eng-oncall.

Kate (eng-oncall): On it. Can you paste the last runner logs and the pod name? Any correlation with a deploy? If we need immediate mitigation we can route traffic to fallback model variant or lower QPS for the affected customers.

Ryan (support): Pod is hosted-runner-5f8c7-gpu-7. Here's the container tail (sanitized):

```
I 2026-03-17T14:02:12.345Z runner: starting request id=req-abc-123
W 2026-03-17T14:02:13.112Z kv_prefetch: mem usage rising 78% ctx=65536
E 2026-03-17T14:02:13.119Z infer: runtime error: received SIGSEGV (core dumped)
---
#0  0x7f8d6c2b4b2c in gpu_kernel_launch +0x4c
#1  0x7f8d6c2b0a9f in attention_forward
#2  0x55a3f8c6 in model_forward

Container exited with code 139; kube restarted container.
```

Mike (eng-runtime): Thanks. That stack looks like a GPU-side segfault in the attention kernel. Two quick asks:
1) Please collect the full `kubectl logs` for that pod and `journalctl` from the node if possible.
2) If you can repro, enable a short perf capture and the NVidia driver logs: `/var/log/nvidia-installer.log` and `dmesg | tail -n 200`.

Short-term mitigation: throttle acme-inc QPS to 50% (rate-limit token bucket), add route fallback to `redwood-v2-medium` (CPU or smaller GPU) for their API key, and scale up the runner replica count by +1 in the cluster to reduce per-worker context pressure. I'll check whether a recent runtime build (1.4.2) rolled out to that node.

Sara (eng-ml): A few notes from model side — we've seen this class of failure before when KV prefetch triggers an out-of-bounds pointer in attention for long contexts (>64k tokens) on some kernels after recent NVPTX changes. Two possible causes:
- memory fragmentation leading to GPU OOM then segfault
- a kernel race when prefetch attempts to build KV shapes under high QPS + large context

If you can reproduce with the customer's workload, try forcing `KV_PREFETCH=0` and `MAX_BATCH_TOKENS=4096` in the runner environment. Also try the older kernel variant (runtime 1.3.x) if that rollout happened recently.

Jia (support): I've already told acme-inc to increase client timeouts to 90s and switch to `redwood-v2-medium` as a temporary workaround. They reported one request where context_size ≈ 70k tokens (they stream large documents). They're open to rolling back if needed but are concerned about data loss.

Alex (product): SLA impact for acme-inc — they're on a Pro contract with 99.9% uptime. We should offer 1 week service credit if this persists >4h. For now prioritize fast mitigation and transparent comms. Please keep me posted on timeline for a fix.

Mike (eng-runtime): Commands to gather traces and coredump (oncall-run):

```
kubectl -n hosted-infer logs hosted-runner-5f8c7-gpu-7 -c runner --since=2h > runner-tail.log
kubectl -n hosted-infer exec -it hosted-runner-5f8c7-gpu-7 -- cat /proc/$(pgrep runner)/oom_score_adj
# node level
ssh gpu-7 -- sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "2 hours ago" > node-kubelet.log
sudo dmesg | tail -n 200 > node-dmesg.log
```

If there's a core at `/var/crash/runner.core` tar that up and upload to the incident bucket.

deploy-bot: Canary rollout runtime/1.4.2 -> hosted-infer (5% of nodes) started at 2026-03-17T13:55:00Z

Kate (eng-oncall): That canary could be correlated — Mike, can you check if runtime 1.4.2 included the NVPTX attention optimization landed last week? If so, revert rollout for now.

Mike (eng-runtime): Confirmed: 1.4.2 includes the new attention kernel switch (PR#987). I'll pause the rollout across the fleet and create a rollback to 1.3.8 canary. For immediate customer relief I'm preparing a hot patch that disables prefetch by default for that kernel path. Deploy ETA ~30m once QA runs the basic smoke tests.

Sara (eng-ml): I'll prepare a test harness reproducing acme-inc trace with long-context streaming. If we can reproduce deterministically, we can validate the patch properly. Also creating an eval to check model quality drift if we disable prefetch.

Jia (support): Customer update sent: "We're investigating 503s and will route you to a smaller model while we roll a quick mitigation. No data lost. Will update in 30m." They acknowledged.

Alex (product): Good. Also ask CS to freeze billing for impacted windows if this becomes >2 hours; flag for finance.

Mike (eng-runtime): Action items:
- Pause 1.4.2 rollout (done)
- Patch runtime to disable KV_PREFETCH on affected kernel (in progress)
- Collect core + node dmesg + full pod logs (support to attach)
- Increase replica count for hosted-runner pool by +1 (infra)
- Add temporary per-customer QPS cap and fallback model route (support/product)

Ryan (support): Uploaded logs to s3://redwood-incidents/3467891230/ (runner-tail.log, node-dmesg.log, core.tar.gz). Links in the ticket.

Kate (eng-oncall): Thanks. I'll coordinate the rollback and run the smoke tests once Mike's patch is ready. If we can't repro in QA, we still roll back 1.4.2 and keep prefetch disabled on canary nodes. Keep this thread updated. :thumbsup:

Sara (eng-ml): I'll kick off the long-context repro job now (job id repro-346789). ETA ~20m.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for runtime/1.4.2 (canary halted).

Mike (eng-runtime): Patch merged to hotfix branch and building. Will post CI link. If anyone sees another node with SIGSEGVs, ping me directly.

Ryan (support): Noted. I'll keep acme-inc updated and log any further errors to this thread.

Kate (eng-oncall): Closing loop when hotfix is deployed and customer error rate <0.5% for 30m.
